master.title: CFD validation of a Thrust Reverser Unit using a static demonstrator wind-tunnel model
master.content:
This paper focuses on Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) methodologies for predicting the internal pressures in the by-pass duct and flow characteristics of the thrust reverser unit integrated in the static demonstrator model tested at ARA in May 2021 as part of the EU CS2 project TRUflow. This paper is the continuation of a first paper on CFD meshing methodologies for a thrust reverser system and three important CFD aspects are further investigated: surface and volume mesh refinement around the thrust reverser cascade unit and first cell height. Four different meshes are presented and the numerical solutions produced for a range of Fan Nozzle Pressure Ratio by employing the k-ω Shear Stress Transport two-equation model. The CFD results show good agreement with the experimental data in terms of the internal static pressures in the by-pass duct. The reverser flow characteristics are also discussed and it is observed that the mesh resolution affects the shape of the thrust reverser plume and associated flow structures between the cascade vanes.


Authors: Bdeiwi H., Preece A..

Affiliations: Aircraft Research Association Limited.

Publication: AIAA AVIATION 2022 Forum, 2022.

candidate.title: The Thrust Reverser Unit flow Visualisation Project (TRUflow)
candidate.content:
For the purpose of efficiency, future transport aircraft are likely to require shorter, more compact bypass ratio turbofans. Issues will arise due to the difficulty in fitting thrust reverser units within the shorter nacelles and so the TRUflow Project is attempting to develop methods to investigate, simulate and predict the re-ingested flows fields around a thrust reverser unit fitted to such a nacelle. Static demonstrator and wind-tunnel models have been designed and manufactured for the purpose of testing novel optical methods and to allow development of CFD simulations. Successful static demonstrator and wind-tunnel tests were held in the Summer/Autumn of 2021. Ambitions are also held for the development of a variable fidelity model and a resulting surrogate model for the Thrust Reverser Unit (TRU) which will greater aid the understanding of such complex flow fields with a view to improving Turbofan-TRU integration.


Authors: Preece A., Bdeiwi H., Ciarella A..

Affiliations: Blue Bear Systems Research Ltd, Aircraft Research Association Limited.

Publication: AIAA AVIATION 2022 Forum, 2022.

llm_judgement.note: Different papers within the same TRUflow project: one on CFD validation/meshing and internal pressures, the other on overall TRUflow project and flow visualisation methods.
